b: Firaxis has released a hotfix for Civilization VII that focuses on stability and performance after last week’s Update 1.5.1.
Saving a game to a network share no longer causes errors.
Fixed visual issues when hovering over DLC options on the Collections page.
Mods that add custom map sizes no longer crash the game.
PlayStation players can host multiplayer lobbies again.
With a controller, the minimap no longer disappears after leaving the Settler Lens.

Specialist costs now grow more slowly per Age, 2/3/4 instead of 2/4/6. Firaxis says this change was implemented in Update 1.5.0 but was left out of those patch notes. A dev note adds that the studio is re-evaluating many per-Age costs “as we prepare for a fourth Age,” and that more of those adjustments will show up first in the Firaxis Feature Workshop.
These fixes, plus some Switch-only ones, will come in a separate hotfix later because of Nintendo’s submission process. Multiplayer and crossplay with other platforms still work in the meantime.

Liberation: After you conquer a Settlement or acquire one in a peace deal, you can return it to its original civilization for a diplomatic boost, or restore it as a City-State if you were once its Suzerain.

Randomized Earth and Donut maps: Randomized Earth keeps Earth’s shape but shuffles resources, rivers, and wonders, with a True Start Location or random start. The Donut map is a square Pangaea-style landmass with separate inner and outer oceans.
Unit List and Map Search: Two new panels, reached from the top of the minimap, for finding your units and searching the visible map.
Great People rework: Great People are no longer built in the production queue. Each civilization’s Great People now unlock automatically through civ-specific conditions.
Still having problems? Report them through the support portal.
Source: the Steam hotfix announcement and the Update 1.5.1 notes.
